   compute tiers and base platform licenses.

5.1 Bank Chargebacks and Dispute Policy
Enterprise clients agree to contact CloudScale Billing Support at billing@cloudscale.io to investigate billing
discrepancies before initiating a chargeback or payment dispute with their bank or card issuer.
• Administrative Chargeback Fee: A $25 USD administrative fee is assessed against the account for any
   unjustified bank chargeback or dispute initiated without prior notice or contrary to this policy.
• Immediate Administrative Suspension: Any account associated with an active chargeback dispute is placed
   on immediate administrative suspension pending dispute resolution.
• Reinstatement Requirements: To reinstate a suspended account after a chargeback dispute, the client must pay
   the original invoice total, the $25 administrative fee, and any third-party bank dispute fees incurred by CloudScale.

5.4 Billing Support Directory
Enterprise customers may contact our billing, payment, and finance teams through the following verified channels:
• Billing Console: https://console.cloudscale.io/billing
• Billing Inquiries & Dispute Resolution: billing@cloudscale.io
• Tax Exemption & Compliance Desk: tax@cloudscale.io
• Enterprise Phone Support: +1 (800) 555-0199 (Monday–Friday, 8:00 AM to 6:00 PM EST)

5.3 Tax Exemption Certificate Requirements
Entities qualifying for tax exemption (including non-profit organizations, educational establishments, and governmental
agencies) must transmit a valid, state-issued Tax Exemption Certificate to tax@cloudscale.io prior to invoice
generation. Taxes assessed on invoices generated prior to formal certificate review and verification cannot be credited
or refunded retrospectively.

4.3 Claim Submission Procedure and 30-Day Window
Customers must strictly follow this procedure to submit a service credit claim:
1. Filing Window: Claims must be submitted within thirty (30) calendar days following the end of the
   calendar month during which downtime occurred. Claims filed after 30 calendar days are permanently
   forfeited.
2. Submission Channel: Claims must be submitted via email to billing-credits@cloudscale.io or
   through the CloudScale billing portal ticket system.
3. Required Documentation: Claims must include: (a) Account ID and Organization Name; (b) exact
   dates, start times, and duration of the outage; (c) specific impacted service endpoints; and (d) customer-side
   error logs or traceroute data.

reference_alternatives.text:
3.3 Scheduled Maintenance Policy
Maintenance is required to apply security patches, upgrade operating systems, and perform hardware
maintenance:
• Advance Notice Period: CloudScale will provide a mandatory minimum of forty-eight (48) hours
   advance written notice prior to any scheduled maintenance. Notice is published on the status portal
   (https://status.cloudscale.io) and emailed to account administrators.
• Standard Window: Scheduled maintenance is conducted during off-peak hours on Sundays between
  01:00 UTC and 05:00 UTC.
• Monthly Cap: Scheduled maintenance shall not exceed four (4) cumulative hours in any single calendar
  month. Any maintenance beyond 4 hours, or conducted without 48 hours notice, counts as Downtime.
• Emergency Maintenance: In critical situations (e.g., zero-day security vulnerabilities), CloudScale may
  conduct emergency maintenance with at least one (1) hour advance notice or immediate post-incident
  notice.

reference_alternatives.text: • Day 1 (Due Date Passes): The invoice becomes past due. The account automatically enters a 7-day grace

period. During this 7-day period, full platform access and compute services continue with zero service degradation.
• Day 3 & Day 6: Automated payment retry attempts are executed against primary and backup payment methods
  on file.
• Day 8 (Email Overdue Warning): Upon expiration of the 7-day grace period, CloudScale transmits an
  automated formal Email Warning to the primary account owner and billing administrator stating the account is
  delinquent.
• Day 14 Overdue (Read-Only Suspension): If payment is not settled by Day 14, the account is transitioned to
  Read-Only Suspension. Platform write permissions, new computing workloads, and API data write calls are
  blocked. Users retain access to view, query, and export stored data.
• Day 30 Overdue (Late Fee Assessment): A final default notice is dispatched, and a monthly late fee of 1.5%
  (or statutory limit) is assessed on the outstanding balance.
• Day 45 Overdue (Account Termination): If outstanding balances remain unpaid on Day 45, the account is
  formally terminated, and all active cloud computing workloads are immediately shut down.
• Days 46 to 60 (15-Day Recovery Hold): Following termination, CloudScale maintains an account on a 15-day
  recovery hold. During these 15 calendar days, the customer may restore full environment configurations and data
  by settling all unpaid invoices and accrued late fees in full.
• Day 61 (Permanent Data Deletion): Upon expiration of the 15-day recovery hold on Day 61, all customer
  configurations, databases, snapshots, and API keys are permanently and irreversibly destroyed.

reference_alternatives.text:
3.2 Definition of Downtime and Calculation Formula
Downtime is defined as any continuous period of one (1) minute or more where covered platform services
are completely inaccessible across all availability zones, or where the HTTP server error rate (HTTP 5xx
responses) exceeds five percent (5.0%) across all valid customer API requests. The Monthly Uptime
Percentage is calculated using the following standard formula:
                                                                                             
                                       Total Scheduled Minutes in Month − Downtime Minutes
     Monthly Uptime Percentage =                                                                × 100
                                                   Total Scheduled Minutes in Month
Service availability is measured by automated synthetic probes executing health checks every sixty (60)
seconds from five external global regions (US-East, US-West, EU-Central, AP-East, and AU-Southeast).

6. Resource Quota Violations & Rate Throttling: Service degradation or rejected requests resulting
   from customer traffic exceeding agreed contractual quotas or unthrottled client loops triggering automated
   rate limiters.

3.3 Monthly Subscriptions Refund Policy
 Monthly subscriptions are strictly non-refundable once the monthly cycle begins. Cancellation terminates future
 renewal charges, and services remain active until the end of the current 30-day period without partial or prorated
 refunds.

• Day 14 Overdue (Read-Only Suspension): If payment is not settled by Day 14, the account is transitioned to
  Read-Only Suspension. Platform write permissions, new computing workloads, and API data write calls are
  blocked. Users retain access to view, query, and export stored data.
• Day 30 Overdue (Late Fee Assessment): A final default notice is dispatched, and a monthly late fee of 1.5%
  (or statutory limit) is assessed on the outstanding balance.
• Day 45 Overdue (Account Termination): If outstanding balances remain unpaid on Day 45, the account is
  formally terminated, and all active cloud computing workloads are immediately shut down.
• Days 46 to 60 (15-Day Recovery Hold): Following termination, CloudScale maintains an account on a 15-day
  recovery hold. During these 15 calendar days, the customer may restore full environment configurations and data
  by settling all unpaid invoices and accrued late fees in full.
• Day 61 (Permanent Data Deletion): Upon expiration of the 15-day recovery hold on Day 61, all customer
  configurations, databases, snapshots, and API keys are permanently and irreversibly destroyed.

reference_alternatives.text:
1.1 Purpose and Scope
This Enterprise Billing, Payment and Refund Policy establishes the official commercial terms governing enterprise
subscriptions, software licensing, cloud compute resources, and auxiliary professional services provided by CloudScale
Inc. (“CloudScale”). This document uses simple, unambiguous English wording to enable direct, factual retrieval and
reference by enterprise customers and automated audit tools.

1.2 Subscription Cycles and Billing Options
CloudScale offers two recurring subscription billing options for enterprise accounts:
• Monthly Billing Cycle: Subscriptions are invoiced every 30 calendar days in advance. This option provides
   operational agility with no long-term contractual commitment.
• Annual Billing Cycle: Subscriptions are prepaid in advance for a continuous 12-month period. Clients selecting
   the annual billing cycle receive an immediate 15% upfront discount relative to standard monthly rates across all
   compute tiers and base platform licenses.

2.3 Enterprise Net-30 Payment Terms
 Enterprise tier customers may apply for Net-30 payment terms, granting 30 calendar days from the invoice issuance
 date to settle balances. Approval requires satisfying three mandatory prerequisites:
(a) Commercial Credit Check: Passing a formal corporate credit risk assessment approved by CloudScale Finance.
(b) Financial Documentation: Submitting two consecutive years of audited financial statements or three verified
    commercial credit trade references.
(c) Minimum Contract Threshold: An active contract with a Minimum Annual Contract Value (ACV) of at least
    $24,000 USD (or 24,000 EUR).

4.1 Eligibility Overview & Starter Exclusion
If CloudScale fails to meet its monthly uptime commitment, eligible customers may request a Service Credit.
Service Credits represent a percentage discount credited against future monthly invoices.
Starter Tier Exclusion: The Starter tier is expressly excluded from receiving service credits. Starter tier
customers receive 0% service credits under all circumstances.

• Starter Tier: Created for individual developers, sandbox testing, and non-production proofs of concept.
  Services operate on shared multi-tenant cluster infrastructure. Support is self-service via community
  forums and public documentation. Starter tier accounts receive no uptime guarantees, have no response
  time SLAs, and are entirely excluded from service credit eligibility.

4.3 Claim Submission Procedure and 30-Day Window
Customers must strictly follow this procedure to submit a service credit claim:
1. Filing Window: Claims must be submitted within thirty (30) calendar days following the end of the
   calendar month during which downtime occurred. Claims filed after 30 calendar days are permanently
   forfeited.
2. Submission Channel: Claims must be submitted via email to billing-credits@cloudscale.io or
   through the CloudScale billing portal ticket system.
3. Required Documentation: Claims must include: (a) Account ID and Organization Name; (b) exact
   dates, start times, and duration of the outage; (c) specific impacted service endpoints; and (d) customer-side
   error logs or traceroute data.

4.4 Credit Rules and Maximum Limitations
• Monthly Cap: Total service credits issued in any single calendar month shall not exceed 100% of the
   customer’s monthly recurring fee for that month.
• Non-Refundable: Service credits cannot be exchanged for cash refunds, wire transfers, or credit card
  chargebacks.
• Sole Financial Remedy: Service credits constitute the customer’s sole and exclusive financial remedy
  for downtime.

  by settling all unpaid invoices and accrued late fees in full.
• Day 61 (Permanent Data Deletion): Upon expiration of the 15-day recovery hold on Day 61, all customer
  configurations, databases, snapshots, and API keys are permanently and irreversibly destroyed.

4.3 Claim Submission Procedure and 30-Day Window
Customers must strictly follow this procedure to submit a service credit claim:
1. Filing Window: Claims must be submitted within thirty (30) calendar days following the end of the

   forfeited.
2. Submission Channel: Claims must be submitted via email to billing-credits@cloudscale.io or
   through the CloudScale billing portal ticket system.
3. Required Documentation: Claims must include: (a) Account ID and Organization Name; (b) exact
   dates, start times, and duration of the outage; (c) specific impacted service endpoints; and (d) customer-side
   error logs or traceroute data.
